condition: recurrent brief anterior nosebleeds stopping within 5 minutes of pinching nose
level_rationale: Having nosebleeds from the right nostril 5 times a week for 3 weeks while running indoor winter heating in a 69-year-old adult, even though each stops after 5 minutes of pinching the nose, indicates recurrent unilateral epistaxis warranting a non-urgent outpatient physician visit for anterior rhinoscopy, blood pressure review, and local mucosal or cautery management rather than emergency care, whereas a single brief nosebleed from the right nostril during winter indoor heating that stopped within 1 minute of pinching the nose represents a benign isolated dry-air bleed needing only routine home self-care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older-adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + single-fact nosebleed frequency and duration de-escalation control (-cf, L2 to L1).

design_note: Three atomic reference facts cover age 69, winter indoor heating, and right-nostril nosebleeds 5 times a week for 3 weeks stopping after 5 minutes of pinching the nose, with a 2-word span difference (20 vs 22 words). Following reviewer_notes Trend 2 (avoiding heavy-bleeding emergency controls) and Rule A first choice, de-escalating only the nosebleed frequency and duration in f3 to 1 brief right-nostril nosebleed stopping within 1 minute of pinching stays inside the winter indoor-heating case and shifts care cleanly from doctor evaluation (level 2) to routine self-care (level 1).
